method: Live stationary scene, sequential temporary A/B changes through developer console. First series: 220 animation frames per phase, first 41 discarded. Second series: 240 frames, first 61 discarded. Values include display scheduling. All changed settings restored and verified afterward. No application source changes.

series1.test: water hidden and all render targets disabled (including shadow target)

series2.test: PCF low quality, water and grass retained
water hidden, underwater pass retained, PCSS
water hidden, underwater pass removed, PCSS retained
PCSS with shadow map refreshed only once

conclusions: Contact-hardening shadow filtering is a major present bottleneck; ordinary PCF nearly doubles frame rate in this view.
The full-resolution underwater scene pass is also expensive: removing only that pass with water already hidden saves approximately 9.1 ms.
Caching the shadow map changes frame time little; receiver shading is the stronger optimization target.
GPU limitation is inferred from controlled rendering comparisons, not a hardware GPU timestamp measurement.
This stationary empty-colony profile does not measure moving-camera grass updates, large-colony simulation, or prove which historical change caused the drop from 120 FPS.

hardShadowFollowUp.method: Same running view, shadow filter set to FILTER_NONE; 300 frames with 61 warmup frames discarded. Water shader still used its previous four-sample kernel during this measurement. Source now also reduces that to one sample. Full reload returned to wallet connection screen, so the combined change has not yet been measured.
